requirements.quote:
Ultimately, servers have the responsibility to protect themselves
against attacks employing 0-RTT data replication.  The mechanisms
described in Section 8 are intended to prevent replay at the TLS
layer but do not provide complete protection against receiving
multiple copies of client data.
requirements.condition: a server accepts 0-RTT data
requirements.why_checkable: The responsibility is stated at a high level and this passage explicitly says the referenced TLS mechanisms are incomplete without defining the additional required control.

requirements.quote:
TLS 1.3 falls back to the 1-RTT
handshake when the server does not have any information about the
client
requirements.condition: the server has no information with which to accept the client's 0-RTT data
requirements.forbidden_behavior: accept and process the data as 0-RTT
requirements.why_checkable: A server test can remove ticket or shared-cluster state and observe rejection of early data followed by a 1-RTT handshake.

requirements.quote:
If implemented correctly, the mechanisms described in Sections 8.1
and 8.2 prevent a replayed ClientHello and its associated 0-RTT data
from being accepted multiple times by any cluster with consistent
state
requirements.condition: a server cluster has consistent state and implements the Sections 8.1 and 8.2 mechanisms
requirements.required_behavior: accept a given ClientHello and its associated 0-RTT data at most once across the cluster
requirements.forbidden_behavior: accept a replayed ClientHello and its associated 0-RTT data multiple times
requirements.why_checkable: A distributed replay test can send the same ClientHello and early data to multiple nodes sharing consistent state.

requirements.quote:
for servers which limit the use of 0-RTT to one cluster for a
single ticket, then a given ClientHello and its associated 0-RTT data
will only be accepted once.
requirements.condition: 0-RTT use for a single ticket is limited to one server cluster
requirements.required_behavior: accept a given ClientHello and its associated 0-RTT data only once
requirements.forbidden_behavior: accept the same ClientHello and associated early data more than once
requirements.why_checkable: Replay tests can target every node allowed to process the ticket and count accepted deliveries.

requirements.quote:
Because clients
do not know the exact details of server behavior, they MUST NOT send
messages in early data which are not safe to have replayed and which
they would not be willing to retry across multiple 1-RTT connections.
requirements.condition: an early-data message is unsafe to replay and the client would not be willing to retry it across multiple 1-RTT connections
requirements.required_behavior: withhold the message from early data
requirements.forbidden_behavior: send the message as early data
requirements.why_checkable: Client early-data policy can be tested with operations marked replay-unsafe and non-retryable.

requirements.quote:
Application protocols MUST NOT use 0-RTT data without a profile that
defines its use.
requirements.condition: an application protocol uses 0-RTT data
requirements.required_behavior: define and apply a profile governing 0-RTT use
requirements.why_checkable: Protocol configuration and 0-RTT enablement can be checked for an associated profile.

requirements.quote:
That profile needs to identify which messages or
interactions are safe to use with 0-RTT
requirements.condition: an application protocol defines a 0-RTT profile
requirements.required_behavior: identify the messages or interactions that are safe for 0-RTT
requirements.why_checkable: The profile can be inspected for an explicit allowlist or equivalent classification of safe interactions.

requirements.quote:
and how to handle the
situation when the server rejects 0-RTT and falls back to 1-RTT.
requirements.condition: an application protocol defines a 0-RTT profile
requirements.required_behavior: define handling for server rejection of 0-RTT and fallback to 1-RTT
requirements.forbidden_behavior: leave rejection and fallback behavior unspecified
requirements.why_checkable: The profile and fallback control flow can be inspected and exercised with a server that rejects early data.

requirements.quote:
TLS implementations MUST NOT
enable 0-RTT (either sending or accepting) unless specifically
requested by the application
requirements.condition: the application has not specifically requested sending 0-RTT
requirements.why_checkable: Default client configuration and send-state transitions can be tested without an application opt-in call.

requirements.quote:
TLS implementations MUST NOT
enable 0-RTT (either sending or accepting) unless specifically
requested by the application
requirements.condition: the application has not specifically requested accepting 0-RTT
requirements.why_checkable: Default server configuration and early-data acceptance can be tested without an application opt-in call.

requirements.quote:
MUST NOT automatically resend 0-RTT
data if it is rejected by the server unless instructed by the
application.
requirements.condition: the server rejects sent 0-RTT data and the application has not instructed a resend
requirements.required_behavior: return control to the application without resending the early data
requirements.why_checkable: A server can reject early data while a client trace verifies that no automatic replay occurs.

requirements.quote:
TLS implementations MUST provide a way for the
application to determine if the handshake has completed.
requirements.condition: an application needs to distinguish early-data processing from a completed handshake
requirements.required_behavior: provide an API or signal indicating whether the handshake has completed
requirements.forbidden_behavior: hide handshake-completion state from the application
requirements.why_checkable: The public API and state-transition tests can verify a reliable handshake-completion indicator.

requirements.quote: Replays of the ClientHello produce the same early exporter
requirements.condition: the same ClientHello is replayed under the same PSK context
requirements.required_behavior: derive the same early exporter value
requirements.forbidden_behavior: treat the early exporter as unique across such replays
requirements.why_checkable: A deterministic replay test can compare early exporter bytes across repeated ClientHello processing.

requirements.quote:
if these exporters are used as an authentication
channel binding (e.g., by signing the output of the exporter), an
attacker who compromises the PSK can transplant authenticators
between connections without compromising the authentication key.
requirements.condition: an early exporter is used as an authentication channel binding and the PSK is compromised
requirements.why_checkable: The passage describes an attack consequence but does not specify a required mitigation or an acceptance rule for the implementation.

requirements.quote:
the early exporter SHOULD NOT be used to generate
server-to-client encryption keys because that would entail the reuse
of those keys.
requirements.condition: an application derives encryption keys from the early exporter
requirements.required_behavior: restrict such early-exporter-derived keys away from the server-to-client direction
requirements.forbidden_behavior: use the early exporter to generate server-to-client encryption keys
requirements.why_checkable: Exporter consumers and key-direction configuration can be inspected for prohibited server-to-client use.

requirements.quote:
Because implementations respond to an invalid PSK binder by aborting
the handshake
requirements.condition: a PSK identity is recognized but its binder is invalid
requirements.forbidden_behavior: continue the handshake after the invalid binder
requirements.why_checkable: A malformed-binder test can observe the handshake's terminal state.

requirements.quote:
if a server accepts both
external-PSK handshakes and certificate-based handshakes, a valid PSK
identity will result in a failed handshake, whereas an invalid
identity will just be skipped and result in a successful certificate
handshake.
requirements.condition: a server supports both external-PSK and certificate-based handshakes and the offered PSK identity is invalid
requirements.required_behavior: skip the invalid identity and allow the certificate-based handshake to proceed
requirements.forbidden_behavior: treat an unknown PSK identity as an invalid binder for a recognized identity
requirements.why_checkable: Handshake tests can separately offer an unknown identity and a known identity with a bad binder and compare the state transitions.

requirements.quote:
Servers which solely support PSK handshakes may be able
to resist this form of attack by treating the cases where there is no
valid PSK identity and where there is an identity but it has an
invalid binder identically.
requirements.condition: a PSK-only server implements resistance to PSK identity probing
requirements.required_behavior: handle absence of any valid PSK identity and presence of a recognized identity with an invalid binder identically
requirements.forbidden_behavior: expose distinguishable protocol behavior for those two cases
requirements.error_behavior: use indistinguishable failure behavior for both cases
requirements.why_checkable: Tests can compare alerts, connection termination, timing policy, and externally visible state for the two inputs.

requirements.quote:
TLS 1.3 takes a conservative approach to PSKs by binding them to a
specific KDF.
requirements.condition: a PSK is provisioned or selected for TLS 1.3
requirements.required_behavior: bind the PSK to one specific KDF
requirements.forbidden_behavior: use the TLS 1.3 PSK independently of its associated KDF
requirements.why_checkable: PSK metadata and selection logic can be inspected for a required KDF association.

requirements.quote:
any PSK which is used with
both TLS 1.2 and TLS 1.3 must be used with only one hash in TLS 1.3
requirements.condition: the same PSK is provisioned for both TLS 1.2 and TLS 1.3
requirements.required_behavior: use that PSK with only one hash function in TLS 1.3
requirements.forbidden_behavior: associate the cross-version PSK with multiple TLS 1.3 hash functions
requirements.why_checkable: PSK configuration and cipher-suite selection can be checked for a single TLS 1.3 hash association.

requirements.quote:
Implementations can ensure safety from
cross-protocol related output by not reusing PSKs between TLS 1.3 and
TLS 1.2.
requirements.condition: an implementation needs to avoid cross-protocol related-output risk
requirements.required_behavior: provision distinct PSKs for TLS 1.3 and TLS 1.2
requirements.forbidden_behavior: reuse one PSK across TLS 1.3 and TLS 1.2
requirements.why_checkable: PSK identities and secret material can be compared across per-version configuration stores.
